flashcards.q: Why doesn't DDP's ring all-reduce communication cost grow proportionally with GPU count?
flashcards.a: Total data moved per GPU is 2*(N-1)/N * S. As N grows, (N-1)/N approaches 1, so bandwidth cost per GPU approaches a constant (~2S), independent of GPU count -- only the smaller per-step latency term scales with N.

flashcards.q: What is DDP's actual ceiling if not communication cost?
flashcards.a: The full model, gradients, and optimizer state must fit on EVERY GPU (DDP replicates, doesn't shard, model state) -- adding more GPUs doesn't reduce any single GPU's memory footprint.

flashcards.q: What does each ZeRO stage shard, and what are the memory figures for Psi=7.5B params, Nd=64 GPUs?
flashcards.a: Baseline (16*Psi bytes, all replicated) = 120GB. Stage1 (shard optimizer state, 12*Psi): 31.4GB. Stage2 (+shard gradients): 16.6GB. Stage3 (+shard params): 1.9GB -- a 64x reduction, matching the original ZeRO paper.

flashcards.q: Why does ZeRO Stage 3 need roughly 1.5x DDP's communication volume?
flashcards.a: Parameters are never held in full on any GPU, so each layer's shard must be all-gathered into a full copy immediately before both the forward AND backward compute for that layer, then freed -- adding roughly a full parameter all-gather twice on top of DDP's existing gradient all-reduce.

flashcards.q: What does FSDP2 change relative to FSDP1, and why does it matter?
flashcards.a: FSDP2 shards at per-parameter granularity instead of FSDP1's flattened/concatenated sharding -- composes more cleanly with mixed per-layer dtypes, freezing individual parameters (LoRA-style fine-tuning), and torch.compile. Reported up to ~5x ZeRO-3's per-iteration throughput where both fit memory.

flashcards.q: Why is tensor parallelism kept within a single node rather than spread across nodes?
flashcards.a: Tensor parallelism requires a communication operation (all-reduce/all-gather) at EVERY split layer -- high frequency, acutely sensitive to interconnect bandwidth/latency. Keeping it within one NVLink-connected node avoids paying that cost at slower inter-node speeds.

flashcards.q: What is the pipeline-parallel bubble fraction formula, and what is it for 4 stages with 8 vs 32 microbatches?
flashcards.a: Bubble fraction ~= (P-1)/M. P=4,M=8: (4-1)/8=37.5% idle. P=4,M=32: (4-1)/32=9.4% idle -- more microbatches amortizes the fixed pipeline fill/drain cost over more useful work.

flashcards.q: A model doesn't fit even after applying ZeRO-3/FSDP2 at max affordable GPU count. What's the next lever, and why doesn't more data-parallel sharding help?
flashcards.a: Tensor parallelism (split the oversized layer's matrices) and/or pipeline parallelism (split model depth). ZeRO/FSDP shards across data-parallel replicas, but at compute time a full layer's parameters must still be materialized on one GPU -- more replicas doesn't shrink that per-layer peak requirement.

flashcards.q: Why do the largest production training runs combine data, tensor, and pipeline parallelism simultaneously?
flashcards.a: Each solves a different ceiling: data parallelism (with ZeRO/FSDP) scales throughput and reduces aggregate per-GPU memory; tensor parallelism handles one layer too large for one GPU; pipeline parallelism handles a model whose total depth doesn't fit. No single axis addresses every possible ceiling alone.

flashcards.q: What's the practical difference between ZeRO/FSDP and tensor parallelism, given both reduce memory per GPU?
flashcards.a: ZeRO/FSDP reduce aggregate memory across a data-parallel group, but a layer's full parameters must still be materialized on one GPU when it computes. Tensor parallelism genuinely splits that layer's computation so no single GPU ever needs its full parameters -- relevant specifically when one layer alone is too large for one GPU.

flashcards.q: If a model already fits comfortably on a single GPU but training is too slow, which distributed strategy should you reach for first?
flashcards.a: Plain DDP -- simplest failure modes, near-N-independent communication cost, no sharding/all-gather overhead you don't need since memory was never the constraint. ZeRO/FSDP sharding is only worth adding once memory pressure genuinely emerges.

flashcards.q: What is the mixed-precision Adam per-parameter memory breakdown that gives ZeRO's 16*Psi bytes total?
flashcards.a: 2*Psi fp16 params + 2*Psi fp16 gradients + 4*Psi fp32 master params + 4*Psi fp32 momentum + 4*Psi fp32 variance = 16*Psi bytes, of which optimizer state (12*Psi) is 75% of total memory.
